newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai first zero coupon bond yields avg 10.13 pct.
newsitem.headline: Thai first zero coupon bond yields avg 10.13 pct.

text.p: Thailand's first auction of one billion baht of zero-coupon bonds was more than four times oversubscribed and produced an average yield of 10.13 percent, a central bank official told Reuters.
The official said the highest yield offered by bidders was 10.27 percent and the lowest 9.75.
The auction was part of 100 billion baht in zero coupon bonds planned by the government to raise funds for bailing out troubled property and financial sectors.
The government approved in late March the sale of 50 billion baht of planned zero-coupon bonds but it later raised the ceiling to 100 billion.
Proceeds from the bonds will be managed by government-run Property Loans Management Organization (PLMO) which will purchase non-performing property loans from banks and financial companies.
Analysts estimated that outstanding loans extended to the property sector by commercial banks and finance firms amount to about 800 billion baht, of which 20-50 percent could be non-performing.
